meta.title: Ch 14: Ind AS 101 — First-time Adoption of Ind AS — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 14 (Ind AS 101 — First-time Adoption of Ind AS).

questions.q: Which is a MANDATORY exception (not optional exemption) on first-time adoption under Ind AS 101?
o: Deemed cost for property, plant and equipment
Share-based payment transactions — apply Ind AS 102 only to equity instruments granted after 7 Nov 2009 that vest after transition
Business combinations — retrospectively apply Ind AS 103 to all past combinations
All borrowing costs to be expensed for qualifying assets already capitalised
questions.why: Ind AS 101 provides EXEMPTIONS (e.g., deemed cost) but EXCEPTIONS that must be followed (e.g., the cut-off on Ind AS 102 share-based payments, estimates, hedge accounting). Past business combinations may NOT be restated — that is an exemption, applied or not.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — exemption-vs-exception wording questions are pure ICAI AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Exemptions: may take. Exceptions: must take. First-time adopters pick up the optional ones, obey the mandatory ones — the names tell you which.

questions.q: At transition, an Ind AS 101 estimate (e.g., useful life) DIFFERS from the GAAP estimate for the same date. The first-time adopter:
o: Restates to the Ind AS estimate; changes reflect new info and are prospective
questions.why: Ind AS 101 exception: estimates under Ind AS at the transition date must be consistent with those made for GAAP at the same date, unless new evidence arises — otherwise consistent; adjustments prospective as changes in estimate.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the 'consistency unless new evidence' rule is an easy 1-mark Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Transition estimates: mirror the old books unless reality (new evidence) demands a change — no hindsight shopping.

questions.q: On first-time adoption, hedge accounting may be:
o: Applied only where the hedge was consistent with Ind AS 109 requirements BEFORE transition — retrospective designation not permitted
questions.why: Ind AS 101's hedge exception: derecognise/designate only to the extent hedges met the original standard's conditions; no retrospective designation of new hedges using hindsight.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — a narrow, high-confidence exclusion asked rarely but sharply Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: No hindsight hedging: transition accepts only hedges that were already Ind AS-clean at their date.

questions.q: A first-time adopter's reconciliations under Ind AS 101 cover equity and total comprehensive income from previous GAAP to Ind AS:
o: Only at the end of the first Ind AS reporting period
At the date of transition and at the end of the latest GAAP period presented
questions.why: Ind AS 101 requires reconciliations of equity at transition and at the reporting date in the first Ind AS FS, plus total comprehensive income for the latest GAAP period.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — reconciliation points are precise MCQ fodder AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Two equity checkpoints and one income bridge — transition date, year-end, latest GAAP year.

questions.q: Consolidated FS use uniform accounting policies; if a group entity's policy differs:
o: Appropriate adjustments to conform the member's FS for consolidation purposes
questions.why: Ind AS 110: uniform policies across the group — adjust members' FS where policies differ (impracticability exceptions only in narrow cases).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — uniformity with adjustments is the exact mechanic AI prediction, not a certainty.

questions.q: At transition, a financial asset derecognised under GAAP but not qualifying under Ind AS is:
o: Restated into the opening balance sheet
Left off the Ind AS opening balance sheet — derecognition is not reversed
questions.why: Ind AS 101: derecognition of financial assets/liabilities before transition date is NOT reversed (mandatory exception).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the no-resurrection rule Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Gone before transition stays gone — Ind AS does not raise the dead.

questions.q: An FTA that misapplied a policy (error) is corrected in the opening balance sheet of:
o: The earliest period presented (with restatement of comparatives)
questions.why: First-time adopters may correct errors only per Ind AS 8 rules — retrospective restatement of earliest presented periods; opening FTA balance sheet adjustments are limited to policy/error events at transition.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — transition-error lane Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Errors get the rewind, even at the starting line.

questions.q: A first-time adopter that elects the optional exemption for past business combinations must:
o: NOT restate past BAs (or restate only some if it voluntarily applies Ind AS 103 to them)
questions.why: Ind AS 101 exempts restatement of past business combinations; voluntary retrospective application (from chosen date) must be consistent for later ones.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the 'may, not must' on restating history Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Past deals sleep unless you choose to wake them — then wake all after your line.

questions.q: At Ind AS transition a company elects the deemed-cost exemption: a machine's GAAP carrying amount was Rs 240 lakh, fair value at transition Rs 384 lakh with remaining useful life 8 years. SLM depreciation for the transition year is:
o: Rs 48.0 lakh (on deemed FV, remaining life)
No depreciation until original life ends
questions.why: Deemed cost = FV 384 lakh becomes the fresh gross basis; depreciation over remaining life = 384/8 = Rs 48.0 lakh. Old GAAP carrying amount is irrelevant after the election.
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — deemed-cost arithmetic is Ch 14's most quantifiable MCQ AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: FV deemed cost at transition restarts the depreciation clock for remaining life.
